name: Construction site
purpose: working at height, permits to work, site induction, toolbox talks, excavations and buried services, site traffic, PPE

scenes.what: the yard just inside the street hoarding, where toolbox talks happen: the plain end of the two-storey cabin stack, the fire point at its corner, the fenced pedestrian route running past, and the block of flats in its scaffolding filling the background
scenes.for: toolbox talks and morning briefings, an establishing shot of the site, the fire point and assembly point, pedestrian and vehicle segregation, escorting a visitor
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs across the yard to the right; y runs from the camera into the site. The cabin stack stands with its end toward the camera: two cabins high (5.3 m), 3.0 m wide (x -3.0 to 0.0), its end wall at y 8.0, running back 9.75 m to y 17.75. Its end wall is plain light grey steel panels with corner posts. Along its right long side (x 0.0): the ground-floor door at y 9.6, windows with open steel shutters, an external steel stair rising from y 16.5 to the upper walkway at 2.65 m, the walkway's guardrail along the upper cabins.

The street hoarding runs to the left of the stack at y 12.0 (plain plywood on the site side, 2.4 m high, posts every 2.4 m at x -4.6, -7.0 and on); a green assembly-point sign on it at x -8.2, 1.9 m up.
The fire point at the stack's right corner, at x 0.7, y 7.4: two extinguishers on a stand (handles at 1.0 m), the red fire sign on its post at 1.9 m and a red site alarm call point beside it.

The pedestrian route to the right: mesh fence panels along x 3.6 from near the camera into the site, keeping people apart from the site road beyond; the materials area further right (pallets of bricks and blocks, a stack of scaffolding boards).

The building: the five-storey block of flats about 32 m away (its face at y 32), wrapped in its scaffolding, the brick outer walls to the third floor and grey blockwork above, filling the background from behind the stack to beyond the right edge and running out of the top.

scenes.what: a working lift of the scaffold on the block's south-west face, 8 m up, seen level from just outside it: a five-board platform with guardrails, toe boards and brick guards, the brick outer wall stepping up against the grey blockwork inner leaf behind it, and the ladder bay with its gate at the right
scenes.for: working at height on a scaffold, guardrails and toe boards, keeping materials back from the edge, safe ladder access, scaffold tags and inspection
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs along the building face to the right; y runs from the camera toward the building. The inner leaf of the wall (grey blockwork) is at y 3.0, with the brick outer leaf being built against it. The scaffold: inside standards at y 2.75, outside standards at y 1.55, both every 2.0 m along the face (x 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and on), joined by ledgers and transoms. This lift's platform is at 8.0 m above the ground: five timber boards from y 1.6 to 2.8 (0.2 m from the wall).

Edge protection on the outside standards: a top guardrail 1.0 m above the boards, a middle rail at 0.5 m, a toe board 0.15 m high on the boards' outer edge, and brick guards (galvanised mesh panels) between the toe board and the top rail along the whole lift. The next lift's boards and toe board are 2.0 m above (10.0 m); the lift below is out of the frame.

The wall: the brick outer leaf is complete to 1.2 m above the boards (9.2 m) up to x 5.4, then racked back to 0.6 m (8.6 m) to the right, where the bricklayer is working; above it the grey blockwork inner leaf with steel wall ties sticking out of its joints; window openings in the blockwork from x 2.8 to 4.2 and 8.2 to 9.6, their sills 1.9 m above the boards (9.9 m), mostly hidden behind the next lift's boards.
On the platform, against the wall: a mortar board on a stand at x 4.3 and a stack of bricks at x 5.6, leaving the front of the platform clear to walk.

The ladder bay projects outward from x 8.2 to 9.8 (y 0.3 to 1.55): a ladder rises through it from the lift below, tied at the top and 1.0 m above the landing; a yellow self-closing gate in the main guardrail (x 8.3 to 9.1) lets people step from the ladder bay onto the platform; the green scaffold tag holder is fixed on the standard beside the gate at 1.4 m.

Cast: the bricklayer standing on the platform at (5.0, 2.45), facing the wall, seen from behind; a second person (a labourer bringing bricks, or the supervisor checking the lift) standing at (7.0, 2.15), facing along the platform or toward the camera. Heads 1.75 m above the boards.

Camera: level with the lift, 5.7 m out from its guardrail: x 5.3, y -4.2, eye height 9.6 m (1.6 m above the boards, as if from a mobile elevating work platform), turned 8 degrees right; lens about 58 degrees across; no tilt; the horizon at 44 percent of the frame height.

scenes.what: a drainage trench being dug across the yard by the back-garden hoarding: a trench box with guardrails on its top, a ladder in it, the spoil heap set back behind, and the next stretch of the route marked out on the ground with paint lines for buried gas and electricity
scenes.for: excavation safety (edge protection, trench support, spoil and plant set back, safe access), finding buried services before digging, daily inspection of an excavation
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs along the trench to the right; y runs from the camera toward the site's back boundary, a plain plywood hoarding 3.0 m high at y 14.0 (taller here, along the back gardens), its timber posts and rails on the site side, posts every 2.4 m (x 0.55, 2.95, 5.35, 7.75, 10.15). Beyond and above it, the upper floors and slate roofs of a brick terrace. The ground is grey crushed stone, darker and wetter round the trench.

The trench: 1.0 m wide (y 6.0 to 7.0) and 2.2 m deep, open only from x 1.0 to 4.5, where a trench box supports it: two steel side panels 3.5 m long standing 0.6 m proud of the ground, held apart by yellow struts inside, with fabricated guardrails fixed on top of both panels to 1.0 m above the ground (a top rail and a middle rail). At both ends, scaffolding-tube guardrails with toe boards stand 0.5 m beyond the box (x 0.5 and 5.0), and the trench's ends are battered back inside them. A ladder stands in the box at x 3.9, tied at the top and rising 1.0 m above the ground.

The spoil heap of brown clay behind the trench, from x 3.0 to 6.0 and y 8.6 to 10.6, about 1.1 m high, kept 1.6 m back from the edge. A length of plastic drainage pipe lies on the near side at the left (x -1.8 to 1.2, y 3.4).

The next stretch of the route, x 5.5 to 11, is marked on the ground with white paint dashes along its line; two buried services cross it, marked with paint: a yellow dashed line (gas) at x about 7.5 and a red dashed line (electricity) at x about 9.0, each with a small timber peg.
The work area is fenced off from the rest of the yard by mesh fence panels on rubber feet along x -1.0 and x 10.5, running back to the hoarding.

trades operatives (bricklayers, joiners, electricians) in hard hats, hi-vis, boots, gloves and glasses

identity.place: A residential building site on a former car park at the edge of a town centre in a temperate country, about eighteen months into a two-year build: a five-storey block of 36 flats with a reinforced-concrete frame, its red-brown brick outer walls rising behind a galvanised tube-and-fitting scaffold. About 60 people on a busy day (the main contractor's team and the trades). The plot, about 70 m by 45 m, sits inside a 2.4 m plywood hoarding along the street; at the entrance a vehicle gate and a separate pedestrian gate with a turnstile; beside them a two-storey stack of steel cabins (site office and induction room, canteen, drying room, toilets); between the cabins and the building a yard of crushed stone with fenced pedestrian routes, a materials area and new drainage trenches being dug across it.
architecture: the hoarding: plywood panels 2.4 m high fixed to timber rails on posts concreted into the ground every 2.4 m (no raking braces), painted deep teal on the street side and left plain timber on the site side, the posts and two rails showing

the cabins: anti-vandal steel cabins about 9.75 m long, 3.0 m wide and 2.6 m high, light grey with deep teal doors, stacked two high; an external steel stair with handrails and an upper walkway with guardrails; windows with steel shutters folded open by day

the building: a reinforced-concrete frame with the grey slab edges and columns showing at the top two storeys, red-brown brick outer walls up to the third floor and grey blockwork above, window openings still unglazed on the upper floors

the scaffold: an independent tied scaffold of galvanised steel tubes and fittings round the building: standards about 2.0 m apart along the face, lifts every 2.0 m, working platforms of five timber boards with toe boards, a top guardrail at about 1.0 m and a middle rail at about 0.5 m, brick guards (mesh panels) on the lifts above walkways, a ladder bay with a self-closing gate at the top of each ladder, a loading bay with a sliding gate; a green scaffold tag at each access point; no sheeting

the ground: compacted grey crushed stone with tyre ruts and shallow puddles; the site road edged by mesh fence panels; pedestrian routes fenced off from the plant with mesh fence panels on concrete-filled feet and marked with signs

safety points where they really are: a site rules board of blue mandatory signs at the pedestrian gate, a fire point by the cabins (extinguishers on a stand, a red fire sign, a site alarm call point), a green first-aid sign on the canteen cabin, a green assembly-point sign on the hoarding near the gate
identity.materials: Galvanised steel tube, timber scaffold boards and plywood, red-brown brick, grey concrete and blockwork, grey crushed stone, light grey steel cabins with deep teal doors, black rubber fence feet. Families: galvanised steel in metal hi, scaffold boards and plywood in wood, brick in brick, concrete and blockwork in wall (shade tones), the ground in floor, the cabins in wall, the deep teal in wall2, spoil and clay in exterior. Safety colours only where they are in life: safety yellow (the trench box's struts, a dumper or excavator at rest, warning signs, yellow and black hazard tape) in the brass family; blue mandatory signs in the fabric family; green safe-condition signs and the scaffold's green tags in plant hi; red fire equipment and red tags in accent; white sign grounds in paper. High-visibility clothing belongs to the cast, not the sets.
inhabited: work in progress: pallets of bricks and blocks under shrink film, a mortar tub and a stack of scaffold boards in the materials area, coils of orange and green ducting, a length of plastic drainage pipe beside a trench
the paperwork of the place, all as empty slots: the permit board, the site plan and drawings in the office, the induction screen, the scaffold tags, a sign-in book at the turnstile
safety kit where it really is: the fire point by the cabins, first-aid signs, the assembly-point sign, edge protection round every open edge and trench, ladders tied at the top
wear: muddy boot prints on the cabin steps, tyre ruts in the stone, a puddle at the low corner of the yard, chipped paint on the cabin doors
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall; a storey is about 3.0 m floor to floor; the building's top slab is about 15 m up; a cabin door is 2.0 m high and 0.9 m wide

scaffold: lifts 2.0 m apart; bays about 2.0 m along the face; a five-board platform about 1.15 m wide (boards 0.225 m wide and 0.04 m thick); top guardrail at about 1.0 m, middle rail at about 0.5 m, toe board 0.15 m; a ladder at about 75 degrees rising 1.0 m above its landing
cabins 9.75 by 3.0 m and 2.6 m high outside, 2.4 m to the ceiling inside; a stack of two about 5.3 m high; the external stair about 1.0 m wide
hoarding 2.4 m high; mesh fence panels about 3.5 m long and 2.0 m high on feet about 0.7 m long

a drainage trench about 1.0 m wide and 2.2 m deep, supported by a trench box whose steel panels stand about 0.6 m above the ground; edge guardrails at about 1.0 m with toe boards; spoil kept at least 1.5 m back from the edge
extinguisher handles about 1.0 m above the ground on their stand; signs at about 1.5 to 2.0 m
identity.default_light: A bright overcast late morning: soft daylight from a high, pale sky, a little stronger from the south-west, so shadows are soft and short and lie close under things (under the scaffold boards, the cabins' stairs, the edges of the trench); wet surfaces show a soft sheen of the sky.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one place (each scene names the ones its camera can see): galvanised scaffold tubes with timber boards and toe boards, red-brown brick with grey blockwork above, the light grey steel cabins with deep teal doors, mesh fence panels on their rubber feet, grey crushed-stone ground with puddles, blue mandatory signs and the green assembly-point sign, the plain plywood face of the hoarding.
avoid: a generic site with no character, or a chaotic, unsafe one (the site is well run; the lessons are about people's choices in it)
real brands, logos, words or numbers on boards, signs, cabins, plant or tags
people in the sets (the cast is separate); plant (excavators, dumpers, telehandlers) only parked and at rest, or as separate props
a tower crane (lifting on this site is done by a telehandler and, on lift days, a mobile crane)
an open edge, a trench or a scaffold lift without its guardrails, or a ladder not tied at the top
safety signs with words; every sign is a pictogram in its ISO 7010 shape and colour
anything stored on a pedestrian route, in front of the fire point or on the scaffold's ladder landings
identity.outside: Over the hoarding and round the building: the upper floors of two- and three-storey brick terraces with slate roofs, chimney stacks and a few street trees; a pale sky; no landmarks or signs.

objects.cabin room: the inside of two linked steel site cabins: pale grey laminated wall panels with slim vertical joint strips, a flat white panel ceiling at 2.4 m with long surface lights, a seam down the middle of the ceiling where the cabins join and a slim cover strip on the end walls, grey vinyl floor, deep teal trims round the windows and the door
objects.permit board: a wall-mounted board about 1.6 by 1.1 m with a deep teal frame, holding a grid of clear plastic pockets in three rows, each pocket sized for a folded A4 permit, a small coloured tab above each (red or green), no words
objects.site desk: a plain office desk 1.6 by 0.8 m with a light grey laminate top at 0.74 m on a steel frame, a pedestal of drawers, a monitor on a stand, a desk phone, a tray of blank forms and a radio in its charger
objects.task chair: an office task chair: five-spoke base on castors, a gas-lift column, a padded seat at about 0.47 m, a padded backrest, two armrests on posts
objects.stacking chair: a plastic stacking chair: a moulded shell seat and back in one piece on four tubular steel legs, the seat at 0.45 m, the back about 0.85 m high
objects.induction screen: a 55-inch screen about 1.23 m wide and 0.7 m tall with a thin dark bezel, on a flat wall bracket; its face a lit screen (paper hi) with a slot when on
objects.site plan: large printed drawings (A1 and A0 sheets) pinned flat to the wall in an overlapping row, blue-grey lines on white with blocks of colour, no characters; the edges slightly curled
objects.mandatory signs board: a small white board about 0.6 by 0.3 m carrying five blue mandatory signs in a row (solid blue discs with white pictograms of a hard hat, a hi-vis vest, a boot, a gloved hand and safety glasses), no words
objects.first-aid point: a green square safe-condition sign with a white cross and a white wall-mounted first-aid box with a green cross on its lid, fixed low on the wall
objects.hard hat: a construction hard hat: a smooth domed shell with a short front peak and a raised central ridge, slots at the sides for ear defenders, an adjustable harness and chin strap inside; white for managers, blue for visitors
objects.coat hooks: a timber rail with a row of steel double hooks at about 1.7 m, hung with a hi-vis jacket and a waterproof coat
objects.scaffold board: a timber scaffold board 0.225 m wide and 0.038 m thick, up to 3.9 m long, with steel bands on its ends; five laid side by side make a working platform about 1.15 m wide, their ends lapping over the transoms
objects.brick guard: a galvanised welded-mesh panel about 1.2 m long and 1.0 m high, hooked onto the guardrail and sitting on the toe board, its mesh about 50 mm, so nothing small can fall from the lift
objects.toe board: a scaffold board on edge, 0.15 m high or more, fixed along the outer edge of the platform with toe-board clips to the standards
objects.ladder: an aluminium ladder with two box-section stiles and round rungs about 0.28 m apart, standing at about 75 degrees on the lift below, tied to the scaffold at the top with a strap, its stiles rising 1.0 m above the landing
objects.scaffold gate: a self-closing safety gate in the guardrail at the top of a ladder: a yellow powder-coated steel frame about 0.8 m wide and 1.0 m high, clamped to the standards, swinging inward onto the platform and springing shut
objects.scaffold tag: a scaffold tag holder: a rigid plastic holder about 0.2 by 0.1 m strapped to a standard at eye height, with a green insert showing the scaffold is inspected and safe to use (red when it is not), no characters
objects.brickwork: red-brown bricks in stretcher bond with pale grey mortar joints about 10 mm, laid in courses about 75 mm high; at a working end the courses step back (racking back) by half a brick each course
objects.blockwork: grey concrete blocks 0.44 m long and 0.215 m high with thin mortar joints, laid in stretcher bond; galvanised wall ties sticking out of the joints about every 0.45 m up and 0.9 m along
objects.mortar board: a square board about 0.6 m across on a folding steel stand at about 0.6 m, with a heap of mortar and a trowel on it
objects.brick stack: a neat block of bricks on a short timber pallet about 0.6 m high, a few bricks taken from its top
objects.trench box: a steel trench box: two flat steel side panels about 3.5 m long and 2.8 m high, painted grey-green and scuffed, set in the trench so they stand about 0.6 m above the ground, held apart by two rows of heavy yellow adjustable struts with round end plates; lifting eyes on the panels' top corners
objects.trench guardrail: edge protection along a trench: a top rail at about 1.0 m and a middle rail at about 0.5 m on steel posts clamped to the top of the trench box panels, or scaffold tubes on posts driven into the ground with a toe board at the foot, across the trench ends
objects.spoil heap: a heap of dug brown clay and stones about 1.1 m high with sloping sides, its foot kept back from the trench edge
objects.drainage pipe: a length of orange-brown plastic drainage pipe about 0.15 m across and 3 m long with a socket at one end, lying on two timber offcuts
objects.paint marks: marking paint sprayed on the stone: short dashes along a route, solid or dashed lines in yellow for gas and red for electricity, small timber pegs beside them
objects.mesh fence panel: a temporary fence panel about 3.5 m long and 2.0 m high: a galvanised tube frame filled with welded wire mesh, standing in heavy rubber or concrete feet about 0.7 m long, joined to the next panel by clamps at top and bottom
objects.hoarding: a site hoarding seen from inside: plywood sheets fixed to two horizontal timber rails on timber posts concreted into the ground every 2.4 m, the plywood's face plain and slightly weathered, the posts and rails showing
objects.crushed stone ground: compacted grey crushed stone with small stones visible, tyre ruts, boot prints and shallow puddles, darker where wet
objects.cabin stack: two anti-vandal steel cabins, one on top of the other, each about 9.75 by 3.0 m and 2.6 m high: light grey ribbed steel walls with corner posts and lifting points, small windows with steel shutters folded open, deep teal steel doors, a flat roof with a slight lip
objects.cabin stair: an external steel staircase about 1.0 m wide with open grating treads and handrails both sides, rising along the cabin's long side to an upper walkway with a guardrail
objects.fire point: a free-standing fire point: a red steel stand holding two fire extinguishers (red cylinders about 0.6 m tall with black hoses), a post with a red square fire-equipment sign at about 1.9 m and a small red site alarm call point at about 1.4 m
objects.assembly point sign: a green square safe-condition sign about 0.4 m across showing white figures gathered with arrows pointing in (the assembly point pictogram), screwed to the hoarding at about 1.9 m, no words
objects.building under construction: a five-storey block of flats: a reinforced-concrete frame with grey slab edges and columns, red-brown brick outer walls up to the third floor, grey blockwork above, window openings unglazed on the upper floors, the roof slab with edge protection, all wrapped in a tube-and-fitting scaffold with boarded lifts every 2.0 m
objects.materials area: a fenced patch of the yard with pallets of bricks and blocks under shrink film, a stack of scaffold boards on bearers, coils of ducting and a mortar tub, neatly in rows
objects.scaffolding: a tube-and-fitting scaffold: galvanised steel tubes 48 mm across, joined by forged steel couplers; vertical standards on base plates, horizontal ledgers along the face, transoms across under the boards, diagonal braces in some bays and ties into the building; lifts every 2.0 m
